answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed on proven misbehavior, turning cheap copies into costly liabilities. Like an orchard where every tree must be planted and tended, a sable-colored ledger of bonded deposits makes identity expensive to multiply. A hollow identity with no stake earns no trust and no settlement, so an attacker must fund each fake agent fully, and the cost of forging a thousand voices exceeds any gain from the fraud.
